S65.12.needs: A paid or Free account that can sign in, a folder that is trusted in VS Code, and an AGI CLI that offers trusted folders (the "Trusted folders" section only appears when the CLI reports it)
S65.12.note: Revoke is in the UI, but granting is not: AGI has no add-folder control in the Permissions view. A folder gets its grant from VS Code Workspace Trust (extension.ts:353 records consent on trust grant), and the 'Restricted Mode' message in localRuntimeClient.ts:118 tells the person to trust the folder. The VS Code trust prompt itself is outside this app's code. The Permissions view appears only when the CLI offers permission rules; the trusted-folder rows appear only when it offers trust. Both conditions are unverified at runtime.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code, then press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Permissions". Press Enter. (Or type /permissions in the chat box.)
Look for the separator "Trusted folders" in the list. Each trusted folder shows its path, with the description "The agent may read, edit and run commands here".
Hover a folder row and click its trash icon (tooltip "Stop trusting").

In the dialog, click "Stop Trusting". Then reopen Code: Permissions and check that the folder is gone from "Trusted folders". Also check that the folder now reads "No folders are trusted yet" if it was the only one.
To grant a folder, open it in VS Code and accept VS Code's own Workspace Trust prompt (not AGI's). Then check that "Trusted folders" lists it under Code: Permissions.
S65.12.where: Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Permissions" (or type "/permissions" in the chat box) > "Trusted folders" section > trash icon on a folder > "Stop Trusting"
